## My Thinking

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. The ground here on the North China Plain is flat and good for grain. I have 10 mu. I know what grows here — everyone around me does the same thing and for good reason: **winter wheat, then summer corn on the same land**. That rotation is what our market, our water, and our soil know. I am not going to try something new at my age when I have a family to feed and loans to think about.

For wheat I will plant around the 10th of October, after I rotary-till the field. I use the improved variety from the county seed station — 济麦22 or whatever the station recommends this year. I apply compound base fertilizer at sowing, then top-dress with urea when it greens up in spring. I irrigate four times: sowing-moisture water, winter freeze water, jointing water, and heading water. I spray herbicide in winter, then fungicide and something for aphids before heading. My father got 350 jin per mu; I get over 900 jin now. That's what the inputs do.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight into corn — no tillage, just seed directly into the stubble. Hybrid seed, 郑单958 type. Corn doesn't need as much water if the summer rains come, but I'll run the pump once at planting if the soil is dry and once at tasseling. Spray herbicide early and treat for corn borer once.

I am not reducing fertilizer. Prices went up but so did the cost of everything else. I will not risk yield.
